findings.description: Calling runWorkOnViaCrew() from the MCP server would corrupt the stdio JSON-RPC stream. runWorkOnViaCrew (scripts/lib/work-on-via-crew.mjs lines 21 and 61) defaults its stdout parameter to process.stdout and writes a 'Spawned <crew>/<member>...' confirmation line on success. The MCP server reserves stdout for the protocol stream. The plan must explicitly pass stdout: process.stderr (or a sink that forwards to stderr) when delegating to runWorkOnViaCrew.
findings.suggestedFix: Update Tool implementation notes for overview.invoke_next AND Story US-008 AC to require: 'pass { stdout: process.stderr } (or a logger that writes to stderr) when calling runWorkOnViaCrew so the spawn confirmation line never lands on the JSON-RPC stdout channel.'
findings.resolution: Updated the invoke_next plan sections to require passing stdout: process.stderr when calling runWorkOnViaCrew so helper output cannot corrupt MCP stdout.

findings.sectionRef: Tools (v1 contract) > overview.list_blockers AND Acceptance Criteria
findings.description: The blocker predicate '(reviewOpenCount ?? 0) > 0' is incorrect. reviewOpenCount is typed as Record<string, number | undefined> (tools/overview-viewer/src/types.ts:89) — an object keyed by review channel, not a number. The current code at scripts/lib/derive-ralph-stage.mjs:64 uses Object.values(reviewOpenCount).some(...) which is the correct pattern. The plan must use the same predicate.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace (reviewOpenCount ?? 0) > 0 in both the Tools table (overview.list_blockers row) and US-003 AC with: Object.values(reviewOpenCount ?? {}).some((n) => (n ?? 0) > 0). Apply the same correction wherever reviewOpenCount is referenced in the plan.
findings.resolution: Updated both list_blockers predicates to use Object.values(reviewOpenCount ?? {}).some((n) => (n ?? 0) > 0) and wrote the amended plan to the requested .tmp file.

findings.description: get_task reads tasks/<taskId>/journal.md but the plan only requires assertSafeTaskId / path-traversal guard for add_journal_entry. An attacker-controlled taskId passed to get_task could traverse outside the tasks/ directory. The read path must either (a) reuse assertSafeTaskId, or (b) only resolve taskIds that match a known task in the snapshot.
findings.suggestedFix: Add to Story US-003 AC: 'get_task validates taskId via assertSafeTaskId (re-exported from scripts/lib/append-journal.mjs) before reading tasks/<taskId>/journal.md, OR resolves taskId only against the known SnapshotTask set and returns { ok: false, error: "unknown task" } for unknown ids.' Also extend Common Mistakes section with: 'Path-traversal guard: every tool that builds a filesystem path from taskId must validate via assertSafeTaskId.'
findings.resolution: Added get_task taskId validation before journal reads, required exporting assertSafeTaskId for reuse, and documented the path-traversal guard rule.

findings.description: pnpm-lock.yaml is missing from the modify list. Adding the new tools/overview-mcp package with its own dependencies (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk, zod, chokidar, @babel/parser, vitest, typescript) requires updating pnpm-lock.yaml; otherwise frozen-lockfile installs (CI, fresh clones) will fail even with package.json and pnpm-workspace.yaml updated.
findings.suggestedFix: Add 'pnpm-lock.yaml — regenerated by pnpm install after the new package is added' to the Files to Modify list. Add an AC: 'pnpm install --frozen-lockfile succeeds from repo root in CI.'
findings.resolution: Added pnpm-lock.yaml to the plan's modify list and added frozen-lockfile verification to the acceptance criteria and verification section.

findings.description: The plan references plans/ralph-pipeline-10-handoff.md but the actual file in the repo is plans/ralph-pipeline-10-ralph-handoff.md. US-010's downstream audit will silently skip the real handoff doc if the wrong path is used.
findings.suggestedFix: Update US-010 AC and Files to Modify section: replace plans/ralph-pipeline-10-handoff.md with plans/ralph-pipeline-10-ralph-handoff.md.
findings.resolution: Updated US-010 references from plans/ralph-pipeline-10-handoff.md to the verified plans/ralph-pipeline-10-ralph-handoff.md path.

findings.sectionRef: Tool implementation notes > overview.list_crew_sessions AND Acceptance Criteria > AC for list_crew_sessions
findings.description: discoverCrewSessions() in scripts/lib/crews-cross-walk.mjs reads manifest.lastHeartbeatAt only to compute staleness; the returned CrewSessionRef (typed in tools/overview-viewer/src/types.ts lines 52-63) does NOT include lastHeartbeatAt. The plan's AC requires returning live lastHeartbeatAt to demonstrate liveness. The MCP tool must either (a) extend the response shape by merging fresh manifest reads alongside the cross-walk result, or (b) define an MCP-package-local LiveCrewSession type that adds lastHeartbeatAt and have the tool populate it directly from manifest files.
findings.suggestedFix: Update the list_crew_sessions implementation note and US-006 AC: after discoverCrewSessions() runs, the tool re-opens each result's manifest.json (using crewName/memberName/role to derive the path under config.crewsRoot) and merges in lastHeartbeatAt, lastSummary, lastTurnAt, listenerState, actorState. Define LiveCrewSession (in tools/overview-mcp/src/tools/list-crew-sessions.ts) as the response shape — keep CrewSessionRef in the shared types unchanged.
findings.resolution: Amended the plan so list_crew_sessions defines a local LiveCrewSession response and re-reads matching manifests to merge live heartbeat and state fields while leaving shared CrewSessionRef unchanged.

findings.sectionRef: Tool implementation notes > overview.invoke_next > Plan 08 dependency
findings.description: The plan says 'If scripts/lib/work-on-via-crew.mjs is missing, the tool returns { ok: false, error }.' But a top-level static import would crash the server at startup before any tool can return that error. The fallback only works with dynamic import inside the tool handler.
findings.suggestedFix: Update US-008 implementation note: 'Use a dynamic import inside the tool handler — `const mod = await import("../../scripts/lib/work-on-via-crew.mjs").catch(() => null)` — and return { ok: false, error: "requires plan 08" } if the import fails. Static top-level imports of this module are forbidden because they would crash server startup when Plan 08 is absent.' Practically, since Plan 08 has shipped, this is defensive but worth keeping.

findings.description: The plan suggests filtering with matchTaskId() post-discovery, but matchTaskId() is private inside scripts/lib/crews-cross-walk.mjs (not exported). discoverCrewSessions() already returns a Map keyed by taskId, so the simpler integration is to flatten the map and exact-filter by the provided taskId.
findings.suggestedFix: Update the list_crew_sessions implementation note: 'discoverCrewSessions() returns a Map<taskId, stage → CrewSessionRef[]>. Flatten the map into a flat array of { taskId, stage, ref } items. If the caller passed taskId, filter the flat array by exact match. Do not import or reimplement the private matchTaskId() heuristic.'

findings.description: Both reviewers flagged that the US-004 AC mentions 'idempotency' for an append-only operation, which is contradictory or unclear. The intended semantic should be specified explicitly: does duplicate (ts, note) get appended again, deduped, or is 'idempotency' really referring to the mkdir of the tasks/<id> directory?
findings.suggestedFix: Replace US-004's 'Tests verify atomic append (fsync) and idempotency.' with: 'Tests verify (a) the append is atomic (uses fsync), (b) the tasks/<taskId>/ directory is created idempotently via fs.mkdirSync({ recursive: true }) — calling appendJournalNote twice in a row succeeds with both notes appended, (c) the existing appendJournalEntry stage-transition tests pass unchanged. Note: append semantics are NOT deduplicating — repeated identical calls append duplicate lines by design.'

findings.description: overview.invoke_next does not specify behavior when deriveNextCommand() returns null (e.g. for shipped or non-actionable tasks). The plan AC currently asserts { ok: true, command: NextCommand } without covering the null case.
findings.suggestedFix: Add to US-008 AC and Tools table: 'When deriveNextCommand() returns null (shipped task, no next step), the tool returns { ok: true, command: null, invocationGuidance: "no next command — task is complete or has no actionable next step" }. The caller distinguishes this from an error condition.'

findings.description: The plan says the tool returns 'array of live crew sessions per task' but the reused discoverCrewSessions() API returns a Map<taskId, Partial<Record<RalphStage, CrewSessionRef[]>>>. The plan does not specify the flattened item shape, especially whether each returned item carries its taskId and stage. get_transcript depends on the caller being able to look up sessionId, so the shape must be explicit.
findings.suggestedFix: Update the Tools table row for list_crew_sessions and US-006 AC to specify: 'Returns Array<{ taskId: string; stage: RalphStage; crewName: string; memberName: string; role: "member" | "lead"; sessionId?: string; transcriptPath?: string; lastHeartbeatAt?: string; lastSummary?: string; lastTurnAt?: string; listenerState?: string; actorState?: string }>. The fields beyond CrewSessionRef are populated by re-reading the manifest file inside the MCP package (see F-006).'

findings.description: The cross-cutting AC 'tools/overview-mcp/ registered in pnpm-workspace.yaml and root package.json.workspaces.packages' couples two distinct invariants into one bullet. Existing CLAUDE.md (tools/overview-viewer/CLAUDE.md) explicitly warns that dropping either yields silent breakage. Splitting into separate ACs makes verification clearer.
findings.suggestedFix: Split the existing AC into three: (a) 'pnpm-workspace.yaml contains tools/overview-mcp under packages', (b) 'root package.json workspaces.packages contains tools/overview-mcp', (c) 'pnpm install from repo root succeeds (lockfile updated atomically; pnpm install --frozen-lockfile passes in a clean checkout).'

findings.description: US-004 adds appendJournalNote to scripts/lib/append-journal.mjs but the AC does not explicitly require that the existing stage-transition tests still pass — a silent regression in appendJournalEntry's signature could be masked by only writing new note-append tests.
findings.suggestedFix: Add to US-004 AC: 'Run the existing scripts/lib/append-journal.test.mjs suite and verify all pre-existing stage-transition tests (appendJournalEntry / formatJournalLine cases) pass unchanged. The new tests live in the same file but exercise appendJournalNote independently.'

findings.description: US-005's byte-range confinement test mentions 'a representative overview-data.js' but does not specify the fixture path or the exact byte-range assertion method. Without concrete criteria, a reviewer cannot verify the test's strength.
findings.suggestedFix: Tighten US-005 AC: 'Fixture lives at tools/overview-mcp/src/__tests__/fixtures/overview-data.sample.js (a trimmed but representative window.OVERVIEW_DATA shape with ~5 tasks and the full set of top-level keys: generatedAt, generatedFromCommit, tasks, phaseTree, cadence, effort, lastTouched, periodic, risk, runs, sizeBucket, spawnedFrom, workstream). Byte-range assertion method: capture the original source string, run editOverrides(), and compare every byte outside the replaced/inserted [start, end] range — Buffer.compare(originalSlice, newSlice) must equal 0. Run for four scenarios: (a) ralphOverrides absent → insert, (b) ralphOverrides present, different value → replace, (c) ralphOverrides present, same value → no-op (assert source === input), (d) malformed source (missing window.OVERVIEW_DATA) → returns { ok: false, error } and does not write.'
